land.text: the Roman province of Galatia, 25 BC

successors.note: Cliopatria's Roman Empire row starts -31; the province was made on Amyntas's death in 25.

capitals.name: Ancyra (Ankara)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Its capital was Ancyra'. Deiotarus ruled 'from his fortress in Blucium' (Deiotarus page).

keyframe_review.note: 50.5 k km2 round Ancyra, Pessinus and Tavium. The infobox says 'Existed 280-64 BC'; the Celts crossed in 278/277 and only after the Battle of the Elephants (275 or 269) 'settled in northern Phrygia, a region that eventually came to be known as Galatia', so the first years are early by the page. The page gives no infobox area, so no area check.
Unchanged (50.4 k km2); the page records no border change in the 3rd century.
50.7 k km2, right for -239..-127. In 189 Vulso's campaign left the Galatians 'free' and 'confined within their own lands'; the page gives no post-war border.

correction.text: the Galatian core, unchanged: three tribes under their tetrarchs (Deiotarus chief tetrarch of the Tolistobogii)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (-126..-78): Cliopatria has no Galatia row for these years and draws the land inside Pontus (see the Kingdom of Pontus dossier). The infobox 'Existed 280-64 BC' and Deiotarus as 'chief tetrarch of the Tolistobogii, ruling the three tribes of Celtic Galatia from his fortress in Blucium' from c. 105 show the Galatian polity continuing; c. 116 Mithridates took 'part of Galatia' (Kingdom of Pontus page), which is not located. The core shape is kept, soft.

correction.text: the Galatian core without the Lycaonia block

keyframe_review.note: 85.7 k km2 adds a 123-cell Lycaonia block (Konya, Isparta; lon 30.2-33.4, lat 36.8-38.8) to the 50.7 k core. The Galatia page names 'Cilicia and Lycaonia to the south' as neighbours; the Amyntas page has Lycaonia as 'the first territory he held' (37 BC and after), and nothing opened gives it to the Galatians earlier. Corrected to the core for -77..-64.

correction.text: the Galatian core plus Lesser Armenia (Deiotarus, king by Pompey's grant)

keyframe_review.note: 85.5 k km2, same Lycaonia block; and Deiotarus's gains are missing: Pompey made him a king and 'the Senate granted him Lesser Armenia and most of Galatia, and he gained part of eastern Pontus' (between c. 65 and 60). Corrected to the core plus Lesser Armenia; the part of eastern Pontus is unlocated.

correction.text: the Galatian core plus Lesser Armenia, valid -49..-48

keyframe_review.note: 85.7 k km2 with the Lycaonia block. Lesser Armenia held to 48 (Pharnaces beat the Galatian legions at Nicopolis in 48); after Zela (47) 'Deiotarus was later deprived of part of his dominions' and the page does not say which. The core plus Lesser Armenia holds for -49..-48; new keyframe -47 holds the core for -47..-38; new keyframe -37 holds the Amyntas kingdom.

correction.text: the Galatian core without Lesser Armenia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (-47..-38): the Galatian core after Caesar took away 'part of his dominions' (Lesser Armenia is the reading: Pharnaces had seized it in 48 and the Polemon I page has Antony giving it to Polemon in 31). Deiotarus died at a very advanced age in 42, 41 or 40; the page names Amyntas, son of Brogitarus and of Deiotarus's daughter Adobogiona, as tetrarch of the Trocmi and then king of Galatia, undated. [Reviewer me-05-d, 2026-10-19: span now -47..-37 (Amyntas' kingdom dated from 36 on the Amyntas page).]

correction.text: the Galatian core with Lycaonia, Derbe, Isauria and Homonada under Amyntas

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (-37..-28): Amyntas, king of Cappadocia from 37 as Antony's client, ruled Lycaonia first, then Derbe, Isauria and Homonada; Cliopatria's -27 shape (85.5 k km2) is the right extent, applied nine years earlier. Cappadocia itself is outside the shape. [Reviewer me-05-d, 2026-10-19: keyframe moved from -37 to -36 to match the Amyntas page's 'between 36 and 25 BC'.]

correction.text: unchanged as a shape, held through 25 BC

keyframe_review.note: 85.5 k km2, the right extent; the kingdom ends in 25, not -26: 'Amyntas fell a victim in 25 to an ambush ... On his death Galatia became a Roman province' (the Galatia page: Augustus incorporated it in 25 BC).

region.text: northern Phrygia round Ancyra, Pessinus and Tavium, the land of the Tectosages, Trocmii and Tolistobogii

ledger.note: 279: Celtic bands head for Asia Minor. 'Two Celtic factions under Brennus pushed south from southern Bulgaria. Per Livy, a sizable force split off and headed toward Asia Minor'; infobox 'Existed 280-64 BC'. They crossed in the 270s, raided Greek cities in 277 and settled in northern Phrygia after the Battle of the Elephants (275 or 269), so the core on the map is early.

region.text: the Galatian lands: Mount Olympus and Mount Magaba near Ancyra

ledger.note: 189: Vulso invades Galatia. 'The Romans and Pergamene allies reached the Galatian lands. The Tolistobogii and Trocmi held Mount Olympus'; the Tectosagi were beaten at Mount Magaba near Ancyra ('Eight thousand Galatians were killed').

region.text: Galatia, free within its own lands

ledger.note: 188: the Galatians are left free. Terms given at Lampsacus: 'cease their raids and stay confined within their own lands'; they were 'not put under Roman or allied control and were left free'; Eumenes II was to set the peace terms. The page puts the treaty with Antiochus in 188.

181: Pharnaces I of Pontus invades. 'In spring 181 BC, Pharnaces attacked both Eumenes II of Pergamon and Ariarathes IV of Cappadocia, and invaded Galatia with a large force'; he took territory in Galatia during the early campaign.
179: Pharnaces gives up his Galatian conquests. 'Compelled to purchase peace with the cession of all his conquests in Galatia and Paphlagonia, with the exception of Sinope.'

c. 116: part of Galatia to Pontus. 'Mithridates also took part of Galatia that had belonged to his father's kingdom'; the Mithridates VI page has the partition of Paphlagonia and Galatia with Nicomedes III c. 108. The page names no place, so only the frontier strip is marked. [Reviewer me-05-d, 2026-10-19: year moved from -116 to -108: the Mithridates VI of Pontus page has him partition Paphlagonia and Galatia with Nicomedes III and dates 'the Paphlagonian invasion of 108 BC'; the Kingdom of Pontus page gives no year for the partition (its only '116' is Ariarathes VI's murder). The Kingdom of Pontus dossier's matching gain must move to -108 too.]

c. 63: Deiotarus is made king. 'Pompey made him a king' (between c. 65 and 60); the infobox's 'Existed 280-64 BC' ends the tribal Galatia. Same state, same colour; the year is a bridging reading of the page's range.
c. 63: Lesser Armenia. 'The Senate granted him Lesser Armenia and most of Galatia'; the year is a bridging reading of the page's c. 65-60.

region.text: 'part of eastern Pontus', location not given

ledger.note: c. 63: part of eastern Pontus. 'He gained part of eastern Pontus'; the page names no place, so the frontier strip is marked.

region.text: Lesser Armenia, where Pharnaces beat Deiotarus's legions at Nicopolis

ledger.note: 48: Pharnaces II attacks. 'Pharnaces defeated his Galatian legions at Nicopolis' (Lesser Armenia).
47: Zela. 'Caesar then defeated Pharnaces at Zela.'

47: Caesar cuts Deiotarus down. 'Deiotarus was later deprived of part of his dominions after complaints from Galatian princes but kept the title of king.' The page names no land; Lesser Armenia is the reading (Pharnaces had seized it in 48 and Antony gave it to Polemon in 31).

region.text: the Lycaonian, Isaurian and Pisidian lands that Cliopatria's -27 shape adds to the Galatian core

ledger.note: c. 37: Amyntas builds a kingdom. 'Amyntas was made king of Cappadocia in 37 as a client ruler of Mark Antony'; Lycaonia was 'the first territory he held', Derbe was added after the murder of its prince, Isauria and Homonada by Roman favour or conquest. The page dates none of these but Cappadocia. [Reviewer me-05-d, 2026-10-19: year set to -36 and counterpart to roman-republic: the Amyntas of Galatia page makes him 'King of Galatia and of several adjacent countries between 36 and 25 BC', and the Roman Republic dossier records the matching loss of eastern Phrygia, Lycaonia, Isauria and Pisidia to Galatia in -36.]

region.text: the kingdom of Galatia: the core with Lycaonia, Derbe, Isauria and Homonada

ledger.note: 25: Galatia becomes a Roman province. 'Amyntas fell a victim in 25 to an ambush ... On his death Galatia became a Roman province'; 'In 25 BC ... Augustus incorporated Galatia into the Roman Empire as a province' (Galatia page).

wars.name: Antiochus I against the Galatians
wars.outcome: In the Battle of the Elephants on the plain of Sardis (275 or 269) the Galatians were beaten and settled in northern Phrygia.
wars.note: The page gives both 275 and 269 as possible dates.

wars.name: Galatian War

zones.text: the Galatian lands: Mount Olympus and Mount Magaba

wars.outcome: Roman-Pergamene victory: the Galatians were 'left free' but confined to their own lands; Greek cities congratulated Vulso in the winter of 189/188.

wars.name: Pharnaces I's war with Pergamon and Cappadocia
wars.outcome: Pharnaces gave up all conquests in Galatia and Paphlagonia in 179, Sinope excepted.

wars.name: Pontic partition of Paphlagonia and Galatia
wars.outcome: Mithridates VI took 'part of Galatia' and divided Paphlagonia with Nicomedes III.
wars.note: c. 116 (Kingdom page) or c. 108 (Mithridates VI page).

wars.name: Pharnaces II's campaign and Zela
wars.outcome: Pharnaces II beat Deiotarus's legions at Nicopolis (48) and was beaten by Caesar at Zela (47).

certainty.note: The Galatians lived in three tribal territories without surveyed lines; the only agreed frontier ('confined within their own lands', 189) is described, not drawn.

notes: Pages: GAL, DEI, AMY and GWAR were opened for this state; PH1 and PON were opened for the Kingdom of Pontus dossier and cited here for the 181-179 and c. 116 events. The Galatia page in the extract is thin: it does not cover the Pergamene tribute and victory (c. 238-235, Attalus I page), the 189 war (separate page) or the Mithridatic Wars. Cliopatria rows: (1) no Galatia shape for -126..-78, the land is drawn inside Pontus; a core keyframe (soft) is added; (2) the -77, -63 and -49 shapes carry a 123-cell Lycaonia block (Konya, Isparta) that no page gives the Galatians before Amyntas (37-25), so they are corrected to the core (plus Lesser Armenia 63-48); (3) the shape ends -26, the province was made in 25; (4) the start is -279 (Brennus's bands) though the settlement in Anatolia is 277-275/269 (infobox 280). Tributary relations: Pergamon paid the Galatians tribute until Attalus I refused (c. 238-235); Galatia was a Seleucid enemy and later Roman client (Deiotarus, Amyntas): recorded only in Pergamon's, Rome's and the Seleucids' ledgers. Not covered by any page opened: where Mithridates VI's 'part of Galatia' (c. 116) and Deiotarus's 'part of eastern Pontus' (c. 63) lay; which dominions Caesar took from Deiotarus in 47; when Amyntas became king of Galatia (the page dates only Cappadocia, 37). Area: the Galatia page gives no figure; Cliopatria's 50.7 k km2 core cannot be checked.
